briefs.headline: Radico Khaitan sets sights on Scotland to secure malt whisky supplies
briefs.deck: Recent disruptions in the West Asia and Gulf corridor highlighted the risks of concentration in individual markets. The company was working to strengthen distribution across other regions.
briefs.bodyText:
Radico Khaitan Ltd. has incorporated a Scotland-based subsidiary to explore opportunities in whisky distillation, maturation and trading, as the Indian spirits maker seeks to strengthen its malt whisky supply chain and expand overseas operations.
Abhishek Khaitan, Managing Director, told The Hindu that the company had established Radico Khaitan Scotland Ltd. to evaluate opportunities in the country but was not pursuing any specific distillery acquisition at present.
“The Scotland initiative is also aimed at addressing the company’s growing requirement for mature malt spirit,” he said.
The proposed presence is expected to provide greater flexibility in sourcing, maturation and storage of malt spirit. However, Mr. Khaitan clarified that the move would not alter the Indian provenance of its Rampur single malt whisky.
“Rampur will continue to be distilled and matured in India, with its identity linked to the climate and provenance of the Himalayan foothills,” he said.
The expansion comes as the company seeks to diversify its export markets. Its brands are currently available in more than 100 countries, with Africa, Asia-Pacific and travel retail identified as key growth areas.
“Recent disruptions in the West Asia and Gulf corridor highlighted the risks of concentration in individual markets,” he said, adding that the company was working to strengthen distribution across other regions.
Radico Khaitan reported net revenue of more than ₹6,000 crore in FY26. Its Prestige & Above portfolio contributed 46% of Indian-made foreign liquor (IMFL) volumes and around 70% of value sales during the year.
The premium portfolio maintained its momentum in the first quarter of FY27, with volumes growing 35.8% to 5.22 million cases. Its contribution rose to 53% of IMFL volumes and 77% of value sales.
Mr. Khaitan said the company was relying on product mix, manufacturing efficiencies and operating leverage to manage cost pressures, including higher glass packaging and freight expenses. Its captive extra neutral alcohol (ENA) capacity of 321 million litres would provide additional manufacturing support.
Beyond whisky, the company is expanding its premium spirits portfolio through D’YAVOL Spirits, its partnership with Shah Rukh Khan, his associates and Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath. The venture is preparing to enter the tequila segment, with the product to be bottled in Mexico.
In the domestic market, Radico Khaitan is targeting stronger growth in South India, particularly Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka, through premium retail outlets, hotels, restaurants and high-end on-trade channels for brands such as Rampur and Jaisalmer.

briefs.headline: Merging SpaceX, Tesla makes more sense for Musk than its investors
briefs.bodyText:
American billionaire Elon Musk’s plan to merge his spaceflight and satellite-Internet company SpaceX with his electric vehicles maker Tesla will concentrate an enormous amount of technological financial power in his hands, with a combined market capitalisation of $3.5 trillion. Importantly, it will create a new integrated AI-industrial conglomerate.
Both companies currently have committees of independent directors to figure it out, and no particular terms are in play. SpaceX has also disclosed that Mr. Musk, the controlling shareholder, will have to approve the merger, although he has otherwise recused himself from the committees’ negotiations.
SpaceX has already absorbed xAI, which operates the Grok AI model, in February while Tesla is developing, among other products, specialised AI chips. The companies have also jointly announced an ambitious semiconductor manufacturing project called Terafab. So, a merger will bring multiple verticals under the same corporate roof.
Eliminate important checks on capital allocation
But, while the merger will ease these operations’ ability to move money and personnel between them, it could also eliminate important checks on how the combined behemoth allocates capital — a non-trivial prospect considering Mr. Musk’s latent fondness for testing the rules.
For example, CNBC reported in mid-2024 that Mr. Musk had diverted 12,000 Nvidia H100 processors originally meant for Tesla towards X.com and xAI, reportedly delaying Tesla’s receipt of more than $500 million worth of computing equipment by months. Mr. Musk later said Tesla lacked the infrastructure to use those processors when Nvidia had delivered them. In January this year, Tesla committed $2 billion to xAI, and when SpaceX acquired xAI, Tesla turned its right to acquire xAI shares into a right to acquire SpaceX shares. Neither of these transactions was illegal per se but they hint simultaneously at the movement of resources and their (reduced) exposure to scrutiny that could ensue post-merger.
A more important possibility is whether Tesla is being moved to within a larger enterprise to finance ambitions that its shareholders have not supported thus far. For example, at the November 2025 Tesla shareholders’ meeting, a proposal to authorise the carmaker to invest in xAI failed under the company’s voting rules. Tesla nevertheless entered into the $2-billion investment agreement in January because the vote was nonbinding.
To wit, the companies significantly differ in their financial circumstances. SpaceX’s year-on-year revenue growth in the third quarter of 2026 was 161% while Tesla’s was roughly 0%. Tesla’s current value far exceeds what its current earnings would justify because the variance is rooted in speculation about autonomous vehicles and AI integration. Analysts have also said SpaceX shareholders could find themselves surrendering a significant share of what has become a highly profitable business to Tesla’s more speculative future earning.
Further, Mr. Musk currently owns around 20% of Tesla but has voting control at SpaceX with 85%. But Barclays has estimated that, depending on the post-merger structure, he could own 37% of the combined company’s equity but 56% of its voting power. That is, Mr. Musk could consolidate control over an enterprise worth many trillions of dollars without also holding a majority of its economic value. One important consequence of that may be a newfound ability to finance enterprises whose economic or institutional rationale is questionable, whose political importance for Mr. Musk is significant, and for which he can skip the support of other shareholders.
A similar issue came up in 2016 when Tesla acquired solar power company SolarCity, setting off years of shareholder litigation. Mr. Musk was at the time Tesla’s chairman and chief executive and SolarCity’s chairman and largest shareholder. SolarCity was facing significant liquidity problems and Tesla had agreed to acquire it in an all-stock transaction worth $2.6 billion but without appointing an independent committee to negotiate. For added measure, SolarCity was being run by Mr. Musk’s cousins Lyndon Rive and Peter Rive. A court ultimately ruled in Mr. Musk’s favour after shareholders alleged he had used Tesla to ‘salvage’ his investments in SolarCity but not before identifying several lacunae in the acquisition process, including conflicts of interest. (Per the court, Mr. Musk was nonetheless served well by having a majority of disinterested Tesla shareholders approve the deal.)
Boost vertical tech integration
A closely related issue is that the merger could increase vertical integration across technologies like communications and computing infrastructure — that many other businesses as well as governments rely on — raising the risk of preferential access and discrimination. (Reuters has also reported the merger could also prompt demands for extensive safeguards around information and technology sharing between SpaceX’s and Tesla’s U.S. and Chinese operations.) Seen another way, a number of services of strategic importance, including Starlink and Starshield, could depend on decisions made within one corporate system that also includes X.com.
Dangerous prospect
A recent example of the stakes concerns Starshield. The Wall Street Journal reported on October 20 that Mr. Musk had personally asked its operators at SpaceX to limit the connectivity of Ukrainian drones to its network, after his as well as U.S. President Donald Trump’s frustration over Kyiv attacking Russian oil refineries. While there appears to be some confusion over who first gave the order — Mr. Musk or someone in the White House — the merger could strengthen the corporation at its centre by bringing together in its halls aerospace, telecommunications, AI, robotics, computing hardware, power generation, and the requisite funds.
The final prospect is as dangerous as it is dazzling: a company that governments bank on for strategic capabilities yet which they cannot castigate without threatening their own interests — the ultimate expression of Mr. Musk’s parastate actions in Ukraine.
Considering SpaceX and Tesla already collaborate as well as can expand their cooperation through contracts, and if their technological benefits are available to reap without merging, those benefits alone will not suffice to explain why the companies prefer or need a merger. The answer, instead, might be what Mr. Musk needs.

briefs.headline: EKA Mobility plans ₹1,000-crore R&D investment, targets 40,000-unit capacity utilisation by 2030
briefs.deck: EKA aims to raise exports to 20-30% of total sales over the next few years. It is exploring further opportunities in the African markets.
briefs.bodyText:
Electric commercial vehicle maker EKA Mobility plans to invest ₹1,000 crore in research and development (R&D) over the next four to five years as it steps up manufacturing capacity and seeks to expand its domestic and overseas footprint, founder and chairman Sudhir Mehta said.
The Pune-based company on Friday inaugurated six new manufacturing plants across Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, taking its annual production capacity to 40,000 vehicles. The expanded capacity comprises 24,000 small commercial vehicles, 10,000 buses and 6,000 trucks.
The inauguration ceremony was attended by Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari, Heavy Industries Minister H D Kumaraswamy and Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, among others.
“EKA aims to scale up sales to match this capacity by 2030,” Mr. Mehta told journalists.
A subsidiary of automotive components manufacturer Pinnacle Industries, EKA has invested ₹3,500 crore in the business so far, he said. Japan’s Mitsui & Co and the Netherlands-based VDL Groep are its strategic partners.
The company, which currently has a presence in Zanzibar and Nepal, aims to raise exports to 20-30% of total sales over the next few years. It is exploring further opportunities in the African markets.
“We are looking at Ghana, Ethiopia, Uganda and many African markets, basically, much of West and South Africa,” Mr. Mehta said.
EKA has an order book of more than 11,000 buses valued at $1.7 billion, with deployments across 14 states. It has also sold more than 1,500 electric small commercial vehicles for passenger mobility, last-mile delivery and goods transportation across the country.
The company is a Champion OEM under the Centre’s Automotive Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme and has secured PLI certification across all its product platforms.
On policy support for the electric commercial vehicle industry, Mr. Mehta flagged the limited availability of financing as a key constraint to faster adoption and expansion.
“Finance is not available today to the extent it needs to be. We have made many suggestions, like make it priority sector or give some kind of subvention or a special scheme to support financing,” he said.
[The reporter was in Pune at the invitation of Eka Mobility]

briefs.headline: Towards recognising women farmers
briefs.deck: Maharashtra’s passage of the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, brings into focus the structural bias against the female agricultural workforce, highlights the need for a database of women farmers and using it to ensure access to welfare schemes
briefs.bodyText:
Picture a farmer. The image that comes to mind is of a man. But when one looks at who is actually farming, she is increasingly likely to be a woman. This perception-reality mismatch is caused by age-old practices of collecting data, designing policies and defining who a farmer is. It makes millions of women who work on farms, make agricultural decisions and contribute to production nearly invisible. That may, however, finally be beginning to change.
In July 2026, Maharashtra passed the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, through a Woman Farmer Certificate. This is the first Indian State legislation to give enforceable legal form to the activity-based, land-delinked definition of ‘farmer’ that the National Policy for Farmers set out in 2007 but never operationalised. The Bill arrives nearly two decades after that policy, and 15 years after a comparable law was first proposed at the national level (a lapsed bill introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2011). It is, in effect, the culmination of three decades of women farmers’ movements backed by civil society organisations.

stories.headline: IND A vs NZ A: India A struggle to break Foxcroft-Boyle partnership after early strikes
stories.bodyText:
Dean Foxcroft rocks back and cuts a short delivery from Washington Sundar outside off through point for a boundary. 
He plays it expertly against the spin as New Zealand A move to 93/3, trailing India A by 253 runs.
The partnership between Foxcroft and Matthew Boyle is now worth 80 runs off 124 balls.
Dean Foxcroft and Matthew Boyle are putting up a strong fight as New Zealand A reach 77/3 in reply to India's 346. The duo have added 64 runs for the fourth wicket and are helping the visitors recover after losing three early wickets. New Zealand A trail by 269 runs.
Score: New Zealand A 77/3 (21.5 overs); trail by 269 runs
Batters:
Partnership: 64 runs off 83 balls
Last wicket: Tim Robinson lbw b Mukesh Kumar 3 (9), New Zealand A 13/3.
Mohammed Siraj gave India A another breakthrough by dismissing Rhys Mariu with a brilliant delivery.
Siraj bowled a length ball outside off and brought it in towards the batter. Mariu, who did not move his feet much, tried to push at it but managed only a thick outside edge.
Wicketkeeper Dhruv Jurel dived full length to his right and completed an excellent catch to send Mariu back to the pavilion.
Mariu scored four off 17 balls, with one boundary. Siraj had troubled the batter throughout his short stay and finally got his reward. It was an ideal start for India A.
WICKET! WICKET!
Mukesh Kumar produced an excellent spell of swing and seam bowling to put New Zealand A under pressure in the second unofficial Test. The India A pacer dismissed Tim Robinson and Curtis Heaphy in the same over, sending both openers back to the pavilion.
Robinson was the first to depart. Mukesh bowled a good-length delivery outside off that moved sharply back into the batter. Robinson tried to defend but missed the ball and was struck on the pads. The umpire eventually raised his finger after a loud appeal from Mukesh and the fielders.
Robinson scored three off nine balls.
Three balls later, Mukesh struck again. He bowled a fuller delivery outside off that swung away from Heaphy. The opener went for a loose drive away from his body and edged it to gully, where Yashasvi Jaiswal took a good low catch.
Heaphy departed for four off 21 balls as both New Zealand A openers returned to the pavilion.
Jurel played some impressive drives and pull shots against McKay and Randell as he moved towards his century.
He then found a dependable partner in Akash Deep. The two batters negotiated the final phase of the day without losing another wicket.
Jurel remained unbeaten on 99, just one run short of his century, as India A finished the day at 291 for seven.
Jurel and Suthar put together a valuable 62-run partnership for the seventh wicket.
Suthar contributed 22 before his dismissal in the middle of the final session. His wicket left Jurel as the only recognised batter at the crease.
The India A captain, however, continued his innings with confidence. He reached his half-century in 93 balls and then attacked McKay with three boundaries in four balls.
Jurel struck two fours and a six in succession to bring some momentum back to the Indian innings.
India A's problems continued as Washington Sundar also departed after being trapped in front by Sheat.
The pacer was the most successful bowler for the home side and played a key role in putting India A under pressure.
With wickets falling at the other end, Jurel took responsibility and found support from Manav Suthar.
Padikkal continued to bat confidently despite Sudharsan's dismissal. He completed his half-century in 101 balls with a boundary through the point region off McKay.
India A were 131 for two at that stage and looked in control. However, New Zealand A struck back with three wickets in the space of just seven runs.
Yash Rathod was the first to go. He edged a delivery from Brett Randell to wicketkeeper Hay after scoring 13.
Padikkal followed him soon after. The left-hander attempted a cut against Sheat, but the ball took an edge and disturbed the stumps.
Ravichandran Smaran was dismissed on the very next ball. He left a delivery that moved slightly towards him and was struck on the pads. The umpire accepted Sheat's appeal for an LBW.
India A got off to a difficult start when Yashasvi Jaiswal was dismissed in the very first over. New Zealand pacer Fraser Sheat trapped the opener leg-before-wicket on the fourth ball of the match.
However, Padikkal and Sai Sudharsan steadied the innings. India A went into lunch at a comfortable 87 for one.
Sudharsan, who scored 41, could not continue after the break. In the first over after lunch, he punched an outgoing delivery from Jarrod McKay but ended up giving a catch to wicketkeeper Mitchell Hay.
India A recovered from a middle-order collapse to finish the opening day of their four-day match against New Zealand A at 291 for seven on Saturday.
Captain Dhruv Jurel led the fightback with an unbeaten 99, while Devdutt Padikkal scored a fluent 80. Jurel was still at the crease on 99 off 155 balls at stumps, with Akash Deep giving him company on 25.
The pair added 69 runs for the eighth wicket in 18.4 overs to help India A recover after losing several wickets in quick succession.

stories.headline: Glenn Phillips on the brink of breaking world record in last T20I vs India
stories.deck: Phillips has scored 276 runs in the ongoing series. His tally includes the 107 he made off 49 balls in the fourth T20I on Friday (October 30). He needs another 56 runs in the final match to break the all-time record.
stories.bodyText:
Glenn Phillips
 will be one of New Zealand's key players in the fifth and final T20I against India on Sunday (November 1). The match, scheduled at Seddon Park in Hamilton, will give the right-handed batter a chance to break the record for the most runs in a bilateral T20I series.
Phillips has scored 276 runs in the ongoing series. His tally includes the 107 he made off 49 balls in the fourth T20I on Friday (October 30). He needs another 56 runs in the final match to break the all-time record.
The record is currently held by England's Phil Salt, who scored 331 runs in five T20Is against the West Indies in December 2023. Pakistan's Mohammad Rizwan is second on the list, having scored 316 runs in six T20Is against England in 2022.
Only two players have scored 300 or more runs in a bilateral T20I series. Phillips will have a chance to join that list on Sunday.
He also needs just 15 runs to break Mark Chapman's record for the most runs by a New Zealand batter in a bilateral T20I series. Chapman scored 290 runs in five matches against Pakistan in 2024.
Phillips already holds the record for the most runs in a T20I series against India. If he scores a half-century in the final match, he will also become only the third player to register four or more 50-plus scores in a bilateral T20I series.
Pakistan's Rizwan and Japan's Sabaorish Ravichandran are the only two players to have achieved that feat so far.

stories.headline: Sindhu makes short work of Anmol in final
stories.deck: The only previous meeting between the two Indians was at the Syed Modi India International in 2024, where Sindhu registered a straight-game
stories.bodyText:
Double Olympic medallist P.V. Sindhu stormed into her second final in as many weeks with a straight-game win over compatriot Anmol Kharb in the women’s semifinals of the Hylo Open Super 500 badminton tournament in Saarbrucken on Saturday (October 31, 2026).
Sindhu, who finished runner-up at the French Open last week, continued her impressive run with a 21-13, 21-16 win over World No. 53 Anmol in a lopsided 32-minute semifinal.
Anmol, 19, was playing in just her second Super 500 semifinal, having reached the last four at the Arctic Open last year.
The only previous meeting between the two Indians was at the Syed Modi India International in 2024, where Sindhu registered a straight-game.
It was a similar story on Saturday as Sindhu’s attacking game, precise net play and wider repertoire of strokes ensured that Anmol could not put her illustrious compatriot under pressure.
Lakshya Sen defeated France’s Toma Junior Popov 21-17, 21-13 to enter the men’s final.

briefs.headline: Brighton stun Manchester City, 10-man Manchester United beaten by Chelsea
briefs.deck: Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first away win against City at the 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title
briefs.bodyText:
Brighton inflicted a second straight Premier League defeat on Manchester City with a 1-0 win to close within two points of the leaders on Saturday (October 31, 2026), while Manchester United slumped to another damaging defeat for Michael Carrick at Chelsea.
Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first away win against City at the 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title.
The Seagulls have never won a major trophy but have already beaten champions Arsenal convincingly this season to show their title credentials.
Fabian Hurzeler’s men got revenge for defeat to City on penalties in the League Cup on Wednesday (October 28, 2026).
Hurzeler felt aggrieved at that result after his side twice led at the Etihad. This time they held on after Yasin Ayari slotted them into an 11th-minute lead.
Bart Verbruggen was inspired in the Brighton goal to see off a City onslaught after half-time.
“We expected a game where we had to suffer. Coming to this place is very difficult, facing one of the best teams in the world,” said Hurzeler.
“I’m really proud of how my players stuck together. They had a little bit of luck but, in the end, deserved it.”
City won their opening seven league games as Enzo Maresca made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola.
However, the 10-time English champions know their results on the field may count for little this season unless they can successfully overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules.
City have appealed, but if that ruling is upheld they are likely to face a severe points penalty and possible relegation from the English top-flight.
“In this moment we are conceding silly goals that we can avoid,” said Maresca. “I think we did enough to deserve something but we need to move on and try to win games.”
Defeat for City means Arsenal can go top of the table if they avoid losing at Liverpool on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
Man Utd self-implode
Manchester United’s nine-game winless run is their longest without victory for 38 years after a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea.
The Red Devils were left to regret not taking advantage of a series of first half chances to take the lead before they imploded in the second period to sit outside the relegation zone only on goal difference.
Morgan Rogers was allowed to run straight through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring.
Lisandro Martinez then did his under-pressure manager no favours with two quickfire yellow cards, the second of which also conceded a penalty.
Cole Palmer converted from the spot to lift Chelsea into the top four.
“The two halves of football couldn’t probably be further apart,” said Carrick, who added he expects to be in charge for Tuesday’s Champions League tie against Roma.
“We looked in a good place going into half-time and then found a way of unravelling it second half.”
Crystal Palace may beat United to a managerial change after Pierre Sage’s side were easily beaten 2-0 at Tottenham to remain in the relegation zone.
“It’s a disaster for every club in the Premier League,” said Sage on the prospect of relegation. “I’m not comfortable with the position but it’s a consequence of what we have done on the pitch.”
Jean-Philippe Mateta’s early red card for a lunge on Micky van de Ven left the Eagles a mountain to climb.
In keeping with Sage’s time in charge, it was Palace’s inability to deal with set-pieces that saw Spurs claim a third consecutive win.
Archie Gray headed in unmarked from a corner before Jan Paul van Hecke bundled in the second after his initial attempt was brilliantly saved by Dean Henderson.
After a difficult start, a resurgent Tottenham are up to eighth.
Aston Villa’s surge up the table stalled in a 1-1 draw against Fulham due to an own goal from goalkeeper Zion Suzuki.
The in-form Nicolas Jackson put Unai Emery’s men in front before Suzuki, who had made a string of excellent saves, fumbled Alex Iwobi’s corner over the goalline.
Oliver Glasner vowed to make sweeping changes after a 2-0 defeat at Brentford saw Nottingham Forest slip to 19th.
Bournemouth were also 2-0 winners over Leeds, while Sunderland remain rooted to the foot of the table after a 3-1 loss at Coventry.
Hull and Ipswich played out a 2-2 draw.

briefs.bodyText:
Even though the Indian team management is steadfast in their backing of the established line, the Auckland shellacking might have triggered thoughts of making some tactical rejigging to the playing XI in the fifth and final T20I against New Zealand in Hamilton on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
India has an unassailable 3-1 lead, but the World champions would certainly not want to sign off with a defeat after dominating the early part of the five-match series.
In that context, the think-tank will ponder whether to bring back Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and the obvious casualty will be Sanju Samson.
The bowling department too has its own issues to deal with despite keeping the Kiwis to below 200 in the second and third T20Is.
India has been heavily reliant on Arshdeep Singh and to a lesser extent Axar Patel for wickets and control after the much-celebrated return of Bhuvneshwar Kumar failed to yield results. The only way to bring in either Kuldeep Yadav or Varun Chakaravarthy is to bench Naman Dhir.
India’s spin-bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule had said that both Kuldeep and Varun were ready to step in any time, even though that chance might not come their way in this series. The home side will take a lot of heart from the efforts of century-maker Glenn Phillips and Michael Bracewell, who made a power-packed fifty, going into this match.

briefs.headline: Crislan’s header ensures winning start for Gokulam
briefs.bodyText:
In the dying seconds, debutant Crislan Henrique, with a superb header, ensured Gokulam Kerala would open the Indian Football League campaign on the right note. And that was the Brazilian’s second goal of the night at the Corporation Stadium.
Gokulam defeated Samaleswari SC 3-2. It was the first-ever match in the IFL for the Odisha club, and though it put up a decent fight, and also had some good fortune, but could not quite match the two-time champion.

The host led 2-0 at the end of the opening half, in which it enjoyed 53 percent possession and had four shots at the target (Samaleswari had none).

The second half saw an intense contest, but Bagan gradually took control and created several openings. Erwin, Manvir Singh and substitute Liston Colaco were repeatedly denied by Punjab goalkeeper Arshdeep Singh, whose timely saves prevented a heavier defeat.

briefs.headline: India complete historic double at Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship
briefs.deck: India defeated Sri Lanka 54-20 to win the inaugural men’s Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship 2026 in Ahmedabad. Aditya Shinde led the attack with 10 raid points, while Yogesh Dahiya impressed in defence. India completed a historic double after the women’s team also won gold earlier. The men finished unbeaten, securing eight victories throughout the tournament.
briefs.bodyText:
India created history by winning the men’s title at the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship 2026 after beating Sri Lanka 54-20 in the final in Ahmedabad on Saturday.
The victory also completed a double for India, as the women's team had earlier defeated Uganda 35-15 to win their title.
Aditya Shinde led India's attack with 10 raid points, while Bharat Hooda added eight points, all in the second half. Pankaj Mohite scored six points and vice-captain Naveen Kumar contributed five. Yogesh Dahiya was outstanding in defence, scoring five tackle points without missing a single attempt.
India took control early, leading 15-8 before increasing their advantage to 30-10 at half-time. Their raiders and defenders continued to put pressure on Sri Lanka after the break, helping India inflict four All-Outs during the match.
Sri Lanka struggled to find scoring opportunities, with their raiders managing only 11 points. Maduwantha was their best performer with six tackle points, but the team could not match India's attacking strength.
Shinde, who was India's top scorer, praised the support from the Ahmedabad crowd after the victory.
He said, “With more and more tournaments being held, it’s great for the people of Ahmedabad too, and we received so much support from them. We hope everyone comes out to support us the same way in the competitions ahead. There will be a celebration, a really big one, and it’s already going on here!”
India finish unbeaten campaign
India ended the championship with a perfect record of eight wins from eight matches. They topped Group A with six victories, defeated Bangladesh 56-27 in the semifinal and then beat Sri Lanka in the final.
The team scored 380 points throughout the competition while conceding just 193, underlining their dominance and making them the first men's champions of the Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship.

briefs.headline: Fakhar Zaman's century powers Pakistan to ODI Tri-Series title
briefs.deck: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by three wickets to win the ODI tri-series final in Lahore. Fakhar Zaman led the chase with a brilliant 127 despite a knee injury and poor recent form. Saad Baig scored 74, while Arafat Minhas added a quick 61 to help Pakistan chase 326 and finish at 331-7 in 48.3 overs.
briefs.bodyText:
Pakistan defeated Sri Lanka by three wickets to win the one-day international tri-series final in Lahore on Saturday, thanks to a brilliant century from 
Fakhar Zaman
.
Despite struggling with a knee injury and poor form before the match, Zaman scored 127 runs to guide Pakistan towards a successful chase of 326.
Sri Lanka posted a strong total of 325-8 after batting first, with Kamindu Mendis scoring his maiden ODI century, an impressive 131. However, Pakistan’s batters handled the chase well despite losing Maaz Sadaqat for five and Babar Azam for a duck early on.
Zaman found support from 19-year-old Saad Baig, who scored 74 runs off 75 balls. The pair added 149 runs to bring Pakistan back into the match.
Zaman, who had managed just 31 runs in his previous four innings, reached his century in 84 balls before getting bowled by Dilshan Madushanka for 127.
Sri Lanka also missed several chances to dismiss Zaman, with Maheesh Theekshana dropping him three times, including twice when he was on 69 and 106.
Minhas and Nawaz finish the job
With Pakistan still needing 106 runs after Zaman's dismissal, Arafat Minhas stepped up with a quick 61 off just 31 balls. Hasan Nawaz also remained unbeaten on 37 to help Pakistan reach 331-7 in 48.3 overs.
Sri Lanka tried to fight back through Asitha Fernando, who dismissed Minhas and Faheem Ashraf in successive deliveries. However, the visitors could not stop Pakistan from completing the chase and lifting the trophy.
Meanwhile, England were knocked out of the tri-series after losing three of their four matches.
